thread:
Sam: quick idea — support fragmented hotplug for safetensors shards so attaching a GPU can hydrate only fragment ranges instead of whole shard
Maria: neat. reduces cold-start. how do we avoid ownership races? full raft per-fragment seems heavy.
Sam: agree, not raft. propose a lightweight lease registry per-namespace. coordinator grants ephemeral leases for fragment ids (short TTL). nodes announce "hotplug fragment fX on gpuY"
Dina: need stable fragment ids across exporter runs. otherwise mapping will break after restart.
Sam: plan: fragment manifest sidecar (e.g., model.safetensors.frag.json) with fragment ids, byte offsets, lengths, optional group_hint. runtime resolves by id. fall back to whole-shard load if manifest missing.
Maria: group_hint is smart — coalesce small fragments at transport layer to reduce syscall/mmap overhead.
Brian: two concerns: metadata durability on coordinator crashes, and partial warmup eviction if owner dies mid-streaming.
Sam: durability: persist lease metadata to control-plane DB with soft TTL; on restart, reconciliation job clears expired leases. eviction: runtime tracks warmup-phase per fragment: PENDING -> STREAMING -> READY. coordinator uses phase to decide rollback vs. mark READY.
Maria: KV/prefix cache interactions? partial hydration must populate KV entries atomically so readers don't see half-populated keys.
Sam: hydrate flow: pull bytes -> write fragment-local KV entries (write-ahead) -> publish fragment READY. readers check READY before using KV keys. this keeps prefixes consistent.
Dina: safetensors changes: sidecar keeps format backward-compatible. exporter (quant pipeline) should emit manifest during checkpoint creation.
Elaine: ops likes sidecar. also need GC for orphan fragments if coordinator crashed — recovery job should scan leases and orphan files.
Brian: runtime kernels sometimes need whole tensor (fused ops). what's fallback?
Sam: fallback policy in route config: 1) async background merge (stream missing fragments and run kernel locally once ready), 2) fallback to single-shard model variant, 3) return clear error.
Sam: sketch lease API:
POST /fragment-lease {namespace, model, fragment_id, node_id} -> 200 {lease_id, expires_at}
DELETE /fragment-lease/{lease_id} -> release
GET /fragment-status?model=... -> {fragment_id: {state: READY|STREAMING|PENDING, owner: node}}
Maria: cross-region case? region-scoped leases + global fallback policy. region B can request if TTL expired or owner lost. need fast invalidation.
Dina: telemetry: fragment_hydration_ms, lease_grant_latency_ms, fragment_failures. send to Optimize to tune fragment sizes/grouping.
Brian: perf tradeoff: smaller fragments -> more parallelism but more overhead. exporter should produce fragmentation heuristics and group_hints.
Sam: phased rollout plan: PoC first with manifest + local partial reads (no global leases) to validate perf, then add coordinator leases and safety states, then canary.
Maria: I'll help with manifest schema and exporter tests.
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: shard-hotplug-handler v0.3 -> canary tonight 23:00 UTC :rocket:
Sam: thanks. I'll open a short RFC PR with compatibility matrix and failure modes, include test vectors (tiny safetensors with 4 fragments). :thumbsup:
